articles.title: Supercell shooter Boat Game is back in limited testing
articles.summary: The Finnish firm’s lowkey shooter appears to be back on the App Store and Google Play in the US, Canada, Mexico, Malaysia and the Philippines.
body: Supercell appears to have revamped its looter shooter Boat Game and is now testing the title with a limited number of players.
The game was last seen back in October 2025, when Supercell ran a second alpha test. It was first revealed in February 2025, when selected players were part of a first alpha test.
When it first emerged Boat Game appeared to be more of a Sea of Thieves-like game, but the new edition is described as an extraction shooter on its app store listings.

A reported Discord message from Supercell’s community team reads: “The reception to the game last year was not what we hoped and we’ve spent this year thinking hard about what experience we want to give players and putting those ideas into the game.”
points: The Finnish firm’s lowkey shooter appears to be back on the App Store and Google Play in the US, Canada, Mexico, Malaysia and the Philippines.

articles.title: Supercell offers Clash Royale players extra gold to encourage their return
articles.summary: Supercell has launched a new initiative to re-engage Clash Royale players by offering them interest on the in-game currency they may have left behind. Named The Royale Interest, this limited-time event lets returning players claim up to 49.6% additional gold, with the amount increasing the longer…
body: The event runs from November 24th to December 31st, with players able to claim their new gold balance simply by returning to the game.
Players can use the additional currency to upgrade cards, purchase new ones from the in-game shop and establish their own clans.
The player reactivation initiative comes after Clash Royale celebrated its 10th anniversary this year, with the title having generated almost $5 billion in lifetime player spending as of March 2026.

Elsewhere, Supercell has been expanding the Clash Royale IP beyond mobile. Its tabletop game with Maestro Media, Clash Royale: The Grand Arena, reached its Kickstarter funding goal within an hour of launching its campaign.

articles.title: Clash Royale recruits creator of AI cheating tool to help catch cheaters
articles.summary: Clash Royale developer Supercell has recruited the creator of an advanced AI cheating tool to help crack down on cheating in the game.
body: AI cheating has become a growing controversy in Clash Royale, with increasingly sophisticated bots reportedly capable of outperforming skilled human players. Players highlighted claims that an AI-controlled account named ‘Clasher’ had reached the top of the game’s global leaderboard.

The situation prompted calls for Supercell to intervene, with the developer addressing the controversy on November 20. In a statement posted on X, Clash Royale warned that using AI or other tools to cheat was a “royal crime,” declaring that offending players would be banished from the Arena.
On November 21, the official Clash Royale X account announced that it had caught the creator of an AI cheating tool and recruited them to help develop new anti-cheat technology.

“The creator of the AI cheating tool has been caught,” Supercell announced in a statement framed as a royal decree from the King. “He’s agreed, entirely of his own free will, to join forces with the Clash Royale team.
points: Clash Royale developer Supercell has recruited the creator of an advanced AI cheating tool to help crack down on cheating in the game.
